title: The Weird History of Psychotherapy Part 1 Freud: A Different Version of Your Dad

sentences.en: Vienna Street, 1866.
sentences.zh: 1866年，维也纳街头。

sentences.en: Young Sidney Freud watches as anti-Semitic thugs knock his father's hat into the mud and hit him.
sentences.zh: 年幼的西格蒙德·弗洛伊德看着反犹暴徒将他父亲的帽子打落泥中，并对他拳打脚踢。

sentences.en: Jacob Freud picks it up, his head down, and he walks on.
sentences.zh: 雅各布·弗洛伊德捡起帽子，低着头继续前行。

sentences.en: His eyes are dull and sad, his smile is dim-witted and dumb.
sentences.zh: 他的眼神呆滞而悲伤，笑容显得愚钝而木讷。

sentences.en: He waves at them, but this wasn't the first time.
sentences.zh: 他向他们挥手致意，但这并非第一次发生这种事。

sentences.en: Freud was ten years old.
sentences.zh: 那年弗洛伊德十岁。

sentences.en: Perhaps he'd heard about these things before.
sentences.zh: 或许他之前就听说过这些事。

sentences.en: Perhaps they'd even been couched in some unwritten lesson.
sentences.zh: 或许这些事早已被编织进某种不成文的教训之中。

sentences.en: From a father to a son, that this was the way things are, or the way that one handles things.
sentences.zh: 那是父亲传给儿子的生存之道，或者说，这就是世事如此，这就是为人处世的方式。

sentences.en: Maybe it was never spoken of.
sentences.zh: 也许这从未被明说。

sentences.en: The man picking up his hat was Jacob Freud, Sigmund's father, a wool merchant who worked hard but never aimed high, and never lifted his family far from poverty.
sentences.zh: 那个捡起帽子的男人是雅各布·弗洛伊德，西格蒙德的父亲，一个辛勤工作却从无大志的羊毛商人，从未能让家人摆脱贫困。

sentences.en: He never fought back, and his son would remember this moment forever.
sentences.zh: 他从不反抗，而他的儿子将永远铭记这一刻。

sentences.en: Not as tragedy, but as prophecy, and as emotion, and as metaphor that he would run from for his entire life.
sentences.zh: 这不仅是一场悲剧，更是一个预言，一种情感，以及一个他终其一生都在逃避的隐喻。

sentences.en: Freud's mother, Amelie, had other plans for her golden boy.
sentences.zh: 弗洛伊德的母亲阿梅莉对她这个“金童”另有打算。

sentences.en: Her darling Ziggy, or little Ziggy, she superstitiously and desperately believed that the universe had marked him for greatness.
sentences.zh: 对于她亲爱的“齐吉”或“小齐吉”，她迷信且绝望地相信宇宙注定他将成就伟业。

sentences.en: In her eyes, it wasn't possible for him to be anything but a heroic revolutionary, a brilliant light-bringer, who would turn the world on its head.
sentences.zh: 在她眼中，他注定会成为一名英雄般的革命者，一位能颠覆世界的杰出启蒙者。

sentences.en: And Freud was raised to believe that, not that he would, but that he had to.
sentences.zh: 弗洛伊德从小就被灌输这种信念，不是说他会这样做，而是他必须这样做。

sentences.en: Years later, Freud would write about his childhood hero.
sentences.zh: 多年后，弗洛伊德写下了关于他童年英雄的文字。

sentences.en: I myself walked in Hannibal's footsteps, and like him, I was destined never to see Rome.
sentences.zh: “我曾追随汉尼拔的足迹，像他一样，注定永远无法见到罗马。”

sentences.en: Hannibal and Rome symbolized in my youthful eyes the struggle between the tenacity of the Jews and the organization of the Catholic Church.
sentences.zh: “在年少的我眼中，汉尼拔与罗马象征着犹太人的坚韧与天主教会的组织力之间的斗争。”

sentences.en: But here's the thing that haunted Freud.
sentences.zh: 但困扰弗洛伊德的正是这一点。

sentences.en: After crossing the Alps, after the impossible march, after defeating the Roman armies, Hannibal stopped.
sentences.zh: 在翻越阿尔卑斯山、完成那场不可能的行军、击败罗马军队之后，汉尼拔停下了脚步。

sentences.en: He stood up the gates of Rome itself, and he hesitated.
sentences.zh: 他站在罗马城门前，却犹豫了。

sentences.en: Victory within reach, and he couldn't take it.
sentences.zh: 胜利近在咫尺，他却无法将其收入囊中。

sentences.en: Even in Freud's dreams, he could never enter Rome.
sentences.zh: 即便在弗洛伊德的梦中，他也从未能进入罗马。

sentences.en: The passivity, the fear, the conflict at superior forces, it would define everything.
sentences.zh: 这种被动、恐惧以及面对强大力量时的冲突，定义了他的一切。

sentences.en: Freud would attach these forces to anti-Semitism and Christianity, and the larger cultural forces where he felt he was not allowed,
sentences.zh: 弗洛伊德将这些力量归结于反犹主义、基督教，以及那些他感到自己被排斥在外的更宏大的文化力量，

sentences.en: and the reasons that he was not allowed to go into these spaces.
sentences.zh: 以及他无法进入这些领域的种种原因。

sentences.en: However, missing the point of his own system of thought, he would not ever connect them intelligently or accurately to his own upbringing.
sentences.zh: 然而，他却忽略了自己思想体系的核心，从未将这些与他自身的成长经历进行理智且准确的关联。

sentences.en: In psychodynamic thinking, which Freud would invent and then strangle in its crib when he needed to, we learn what makes us lovable from the parent of the opposite sex.
sentences.zh: 在心理动力学思想中——这是弗洛伊德发明的，但在需要时又被他亲手扼杀的理论——我们从异性父母那里学会了什么让我们变得可爱。

sentences.en: But we learn how to be in the world, or our coping style, from the parent of the same sex.
sentences.zh: 但我们从同性父母那里学会了如何立足于世，即我们的应对风格。

sentences.en: From his mother, greatness equaled love.
sentences.zh: 从母亲那里，他学会了伟大等同于爱。

sentences.en: From his father, Freud learned to submit and conform and avoid any type of conflict.
sentences.zh: 从父亲那里，弗洛伊德学会了顺从、妥协以及回避任何形式的冲突。

sentences.en: This extreme passivity Freud absorbed made him repress every competitive or aggressive impulse.
sentences.zh: 弗洛伊德所吸收的这种极端被动性，使他压抑了所有的竞争或攻击冲动。

sentences.en: Freud would never connect the ambivalence between the need to hide from God and the need to be God, or the desire to disappear and not have to fight with the need to fight.
sentences.zh: 弗洛伊德从未将那种“既要躲避上帝又要成为上帝”的矛盾心理，或者“想要消失、无需抗争”与“必须抗争”的渴望联系起来。

sentences.en: But the inability to handle anger, whether or not we handle it in an outward way or an internal way, is the same thing.
sentences.zh: 但无论我们是以向外还是向内的方式处理愤怒，无法应对愤怒的本质是一样的。

sentences.en: And Freud would never realize that even though he handled his phobias, his neuroses, whatever you want to call them, I would call them, an avoidance of an emotional arc,
sentences.zh: 弗洛伊德从未意识到，尽管他处理恐惧症、神经症——或者随你怎么称呼它们，我称之为对情感弧线的回避——的方式与他父亲不同，

sentences.en: differently from his father, that he was still ruled for his entire life by the same thing.
sentences.zh: 但他终其一生仍被同样的东西所统治。

sentences.en: That had ruled Jacob.
sentences.zh: 统治着雅各布的那种东西。

sentences.en: So, naturally, this repressed aggression became the cornerstone of his psychology, and we diagnose in others what we can't admit in ourselves.
sentences.zh: 因此，这种被压抑的攻击性自然成为了他心理学的基石，我们往往在他人身上诊断出我们自己无法承认的东西。

sentences.en: As Joseph Campbell would later point out,
sentences.zh: 正如约瑟夫·坎贝尔后来指出的那样，

sentences.en: Freud was fishing while he sat on a whale.
sentences.zh: 弗洛伊德坐在鲸鱼背上垂钓。

sentences.en: Freud prided himself on being bold, revolutionary.
sentences.zh: 弗洛伊德以大胆、革命自居。

sentences.en: Read his letters.
sentences.zh: 去读读他的信件吧。

sentences.en: It's all self-deception.
sentences.zh: 那全是自我欺骗。

sentences.en: When he disagreed with his friends or mentors, he didn't argue for compromise, and rarely did he ever confront them.
sentences.zh: 当他与朋友或导师意见不合时，他从不寻求妥协，也极少与他们正面交锋。

sentences.en: Oftentimes, he developed a very deep internal self-loathing while appearing overly facile, supplicatory, and sort of like negotiating with them
sentences.zh: 很多时候，他会产生极深的内在自我厌恶，表面上却显得过于圆滑、卑微，仿佛在与他们谈判，

sentences.en: or complimenting them while he hated them.
sentences.zh: 或者在憎恨他们的同时还要恭维他们。

sentences.en: Most of the time, he simply cut them off.
sentences.zh: 大多数时候，他只是简单地切断与他们的联系。

sentences.en: Jung, Adler, Rank.
sentences.zh: 荣格、阿德勒、兰克。

sentences.en: First, they were worshipped, and then they were discarded.
sentences.zh: 起初他们被奉为神明，随后又被弃之如敝履。

sentences.en: Brewer, Fleece, Charcot.
sentences.zh: 布洛伊尔、弗利斯、沙可。

sentences.en: They were adopted fathers until they disappointed him.
sentences.zh: 他们曾是他的代父，直到他们让他失望。

sentences.en: Take his golden boy period, you know, with Carl Jung.
sentences.zh: 以他与卡尔·荣格的“金童”时期为例。

sentences.en: They were discussing a patient's dream.
sentences.zh: 他们当时正在讨论一位病人的梦。

sentences.en: Jung offers a different interpretation of the dream than his own dream, right?
sentences.zh: 荣格提出了与他自己不同的梦境解读，对吧？

sentences.en: It's Jung's dream.
sentences.zh: 那是荣格的梦。

sentences.en: And Freud turns white, and he shakes, and he faints, and he falls to the floor.
sentences.zh: 弗洛伊德脸色惨白，浑身颤抖，随后晕倒在地。

sentences.en: And he tells Jung that this interpretation cannot be true.
sentences.zh: 他告诉荣格，这种解读绝不可能是真的。

sentences.en: Freud tells Jung that both the contra-interpretation of his dream and the bog bodies that they're about to see the exhibit of in Vienna
sentences.zh: 弗洛伊德告诉荣格，无论是对他梦境的反向解读，还是他们即将去维也纳参观展览中提到的沼泽尸体，

sentences.en: that Jung has mentioned mean that Jung has a death wish against Freud,
sentences.zh: 荣格提到的这些都意味着荣格对弗洛伊德怀有杀意，

sentences.en: simply because Jung had a willingness to think for himself.
sentences.zh: 仅仅因为荣格有独立思考的意愿。

sentences.en: That would kill the image of perfection that Freud needed to feel lovable.
sentences.zh: 这会摧毁弗洛伊德为了感到被爱而必须维持的完美形象。

sentences.en: This is someone who, throughout their entire career,
sentences.zh: 这就是一个贯穿其整个职业生涯的人，

sentences.en: if you want to sit with this idea that we become lovable from the parent of the opposite sex, meaning not necessarily what makes us lovable all the time,
sentences.zh: 如果你想接受这个观点：我们从异性父母那里变得可爱，这并不一定意味着什么让我们一直可爱，

sentences.en: but a lot of times what informs our purpose.
sentences.zh: 但很多时候这决定了我们的目标。

sentences.en: To be an artist, to be an innovator, to be a discoverer, to see through the lies of society, to be a hard worker, to be somebody who conforms to the rules
sentences.zh: 成为艺术家、创新者、发现者，看穿社会的谎言，成为勤奋工作的人，成为遵守规则的人，

sentences.en: as a point of order, as a point of pride, whatever that is,
sentences.zh: 作为一种秩序，作为一种骄傲，无论那是什么，

sentences.en: often is at odds with the way we learn to be in the world from the parent of the same sex.
sentences.zh: 往往与我们从同性父母那里学到的立世之道相冲突。

sentences.en: We learn what makes our purpose from the parent of the opposite sex, but how to be in the world,
sentences.zh: 我们从异性父母那里学会了目标是什么，但如何立足于世，

sentences.en: or what our coping style is from the parent of the same sex.
sentences.zh: 或者我们的应对风格，则是从同性父母那里学来的。

sentences.en: And a lot of times, especially if you're a wounded healer, like most therapists, these things are at odds.
sentences.zh: 很多时候，特别是如果你像大多数治疗师一样是一位“受伤的疗愈者”，这两者是冲突的。

sentences.en: Sometimes we learn to be over-antagonistic from the parent of the same sex, or we learn as our coping style to performatively seek victimhood or the lost cause of the great person
sentences.zh: 有时我们从同性父母那里学会了过度对抗，或者我们将表演性地寻求受害者身份、追求伟人的失败事业作为应对风格，

sentences.en: that will ultimately be undone, or to simply shut down and then cry out and receive help from a parent.
sentences.zh: 最终导致失败，或者干脆封闭自己，然后大声呼救以获得父母的帮助。

sentences.en: But Freud needed to be the most brilliant person in the room.
sentences.zh: 但弗洛伊德需要成为房间里最聪明的人。

sentences.en: But he also couldn't really fight with anyone.
sentences.zh: 可他实际上又无法与任何人发生争执。

sentences.en: And so he had to continue to back up until he had an all-encompassing system of understanding where his brilliance preceded him and his authority was presupposed by everyone
sentences.zh: 因此他不得不不断退缩，直到建立起一套包罗万象的理解体系，让他的才华先于他本人，让他的权威被所有人预设，

sentences.en: because he couldn't have conflict.
sentences.zh: 因为他无法处理冲突。

sentences.en: Cut to Vienna, 1844.
sentences.zh: 转场到1844年的维也纳。

sentences.en: Freud's first and last love wasn't a woman or an idea.
sentences.zh: 弗洛伊德的初恋也是他最后的爱，不是女人，也不是某种理念。

sentences.en: It was cocaine.
sentences.zh: 而是可卡因。

sentences.en: He starts researching it in 1884 and convinced that he found this miracle cure,
sentences.zh: 他在1884年开始研究它，并确信自己找到了这种灵丹妙药，

sentences.en: his colleague Carl Kohler is searching for this topical anesthetic, you know, crucial for eye surgery, in an era before general anesthesia.
sentences.zh: 他的同事卡尔·科勒正在寻找一种局部麻醉剂，这在没有全身麻醉的时代对于眼科手术至关重要。

sentences.en: When you cut on people in a time before antibiotics and a time before anesthesia to do surgery, they tend to do something that is sort of inconvenient
sentences.zh: 在抗生素和麻醉技术出现之前的时代进行手术时，病人往往会做出一些让外科医生感到不便的行为，

sentences.en: for the surgeon, like be awake and squirm around and have involuntary reactions to pain.
sentences.zh: 比如保持清醒、扭动身体，以及对疼痛产生不由自主的反应。

sentences.en: Freud suggests cocaine, and it works.
sentences.zh: 弗洛伊德建议使用可卡因，结果奏效了。

sentences.en: It was one of the decade's biggest medical discoveries.
sentences.zh: 这是那个十年中最伟大的医学发现之一。

sentences.en: But what does Freud do?
sentences.zh: 但弗洛伊德做了什么？

sentences.en: First, he congratulates Kohler, even though he feels like it's stolen while he's visiting his fiancée.
sentences.zh: 起初，他祝贺了科勒，尽管他在拜访未婚妻时觉得这成果被窃取了。

sentences.en: So he plants rumors that Kohler stole the discovery from his notes, even though it was freely given, and Freud probably didn't understand the implications
sentences.zh: 于是他散布谣言说科勒从他的笔记中窃取了这一发现，尽管那是他主动分享的，而且弗洛伊德在当时可能并未理解该发现的深远意义，

sentences.en: of that discovery when it happens, or his own insight.
sentences.zh: 或者他自己的洞见。

sentences.en: And Kohler also freely gave Freud credit, even though he published the paper.
sentences.zh: 科勒也大方地将功劳归于弗洛伊德，尽管论文是他发表的。

sentences.en: The slander follows Kohler's ophthalmology career, you know, to America for the rest of his life, another discarded father figure that Jung would collect,
sentences.zh: 诽谤伴随着科勒的眼科生涯，甚至追随他到了美国，这是荣格会收集的又一个被抛弃的父亲形象，

sentences.en: just like another discarded son figure that he would never ultimately be able to craft the perfect son, just like he could never craft himself into the perfect father.
sentences.zh: 就像他永远无法塑造出完美的儿子一样，正如他永远无法将自己塑造成完美的父亲。

sentences.en: And this starts this pattern.
sentences.zh: 这开启了一种模式。

sentences.en: Freud courts father figures, and then he destroys them.
sentences.zh: 弗洛伊德追逐父亲形象，然后摧毁他们。

sentences.en: And it also starts Freud's solution to every problem for a while, which is cocaine.
sentences.zh: 这也开启了弗洛伊德一段时间内解决所有问题的方案，那就是可卡因。

sentences.en: Freud starts, he switches careers at this point.
sentences.zh: 弗洛伊德在此时转换了职业方向。

sentences.en: There will not be a bigger discovery in surgery.
sentences.zh: 外科手术领域不会再有比这更大的发现了。

sentences.en: There can't be.
sentences.zh: 不可能有了。

sentences.en: Kohler's taken it, and so Freud enters neurology.
sentences.zh: 科勒已经拿走了，于是弗洛伊德进入了神经学领域。

sentences.en: And he begins treating depressed patients by injecting them with cocaine and asking them how they feel.
sentences.zh: 他开始通过注射可卡因来治疗抑郁症患者，并询问他们的感受。

sentences.en: And typically they feel great, so he publishes triumphantly.
sentences.zh: 通常他们感觉很好，于是他得意洋洋地发表了成果。

sentences.en: Cocaine became the first wonderful, you know, revelation in surgery, but I had to leave that field because I am the darling and precious Ziggy,
sentences.zh: 可卡因成了外科手术中第一个美妙的启示，但我不得不离开那个领域，因为我是那个珍贵的小齐吉，

sentences.en: who is the most brilliant, and now I can never be known for that, so I have to bring this to another field.
sentences.zh: 我是最聪明的，现在我不能因为那个而闻名，所以我必须把它带到另一个领域。

sentences.en: But several patients get addicted to cotang like one does, and then in one of his close friends, Ernst von Fleischel, he dies horribly.
sentences.zh: 但几位病人像常人一样对可卡因上瘾了，后来他的一位密友恩斯特·冯·弗莱舍尔死得非常惨。

sentences.en: And Freud never publishes objective research again
sentences.zh: 从此弗洛伊德再也没有发表过客观的研究成果，

sentences.en: because when he takes a risk with a real study about a real drug in an objective way, it hurts him.
sentences.zh: 因为当他以客观方式对真实药物进行真实研究并承担风险时，这伤害了他。

sentences.en: He becomes disgraced.
sentences.zh: 他名誉扫地。

sentences.en: And Freud never publishes in that way.
sentences.zh: 弗洛伊德再也没有那样发表过文章。

sentences.en: He transforms himself into something different that is inherently subjective, inherently slippery, beneath the rules of empiricism.
sentences.zh: 他将自己转变成了一种本质上主观的、本质上难以捉摸的、凌驾于经验主义规则之上的存在。

sentences.en: Dr. Frederick Cruz's book on this,
sentences.zh: 弗雷德里克·克鲁兹博士关于此事的书，

sentences.en: Freud's Making of an Illusion, is a good one.
sentences.zh: 《弗洛伊德：幻觉的制造》，是一本好书。

sentences.en: I've said before on the blog, he was a pen pal of mine before his death, and we had the same enemies.
sentences.zh: 我之前在博客上说过，他在去世前曾是我的笔友，我们有着共同的敌人。

sentences.en: I enjoyed corresponding with him quite a bit.
sentences.zh: 我非常享受与他的通信。

sentences.en: Props to him.
sentences.zh: 向他致敬。

sentences.en: You should read the book.
sentences.zh: 你应该读读这本书。

sentences.en: A lot of the newer work on Freud.
sentences.zh: 关于弗洛伊德的许多新研究。

sentences.en: It's probably the best new work on Freud because even the best biographies of Freud didn't have the information that we have now simply because a lot of these things
sentences.zh: 这可能是关于弗洛伊德最好的新作品，因为即使是最好的弗洛伊德传记也没有我们现在掌握的信息，仅仅是因为其中许多事情，

sentences.en: were still covered up by the descendants of Freud until relatively recently.
sentences.zh: 直到相对近期才被弗洛伊德的后代掩盖。

sentences.en: It's a good book.
sentences.zh: 这是一本好书。
